carry: Instrument defect, observed 2026-10-20 (orchestrator): tools/audit/worktree_gc.sh collected the roster worktree while it held an unpushed commit on the roster branch, and deleted the branch with it. The tool's own header promises a worktree with unpushed work is left alone. What happened: roster_edit.py committed set-stage for R10-STAMP at 247fbcc7 with "nothing pushed" on handoff/audit-r10-roster, worktree_gc ran in the same minute, and the worktree (~/hpo-seats/r10s3/roster-r10) and the local branch were both gone; the commit survived only as a loose object, and `git push 247fbcc7:refs/heads/handoff/audit-r10-roster` fast-forwarded the remote from 982a942, which proves it was unpushed. Nothing was lost only because the object had not been gc'd. Control for the fix: a worktree checked out on a branch with exactly one unpushed commit must be kept by both the classify and the apply paths, and the self-test must plant that case and fail without the clause; null control: a clean worktree at a merged head is still collected. Re-measure at your base: create the case in a scratch clone, run worktree_gc --dry-run and --apply, and read the summary line.
brief: Fly-in carved out of R10-ORCH-MACHINERY's re-cut (orchestrator decision under mandate 6329234399, 2026-10-23; note on design/R10-ORCH-MACHINERY at 2fc665c61, section 3 row G): one module, one defect, no dependency on the ledger, beat or page. worktree_gc.sh must leave alone a worktree holding an unpushed commit, as its header promises (the carry has the instance). Follow dev/governance/roles/fixer.md: failing test first, mutation proof, the finder's harness at both ends, a null control for every quantified claim, the scoped gate and the structure ratchet before the push.
